Tofu Cajun Fajita Burrito

50 min · serves 4
vegantofuwrapdinnerspicyhigh protein

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Da3IbwZxS9L/

Ingredients

Tofu Filling

  • 1 block extra-firm tofu, diced
  • 2 bell peppers of choice, sliced
  • ½ red onion, sliced
  • 1–2 jalapeños, sliced
  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning
  • ½ tbsp onion powder
  • ¼ tsp salt (or more to taste)
  • Juice of ½ lime
  • A handful of shredded vegan mozzarella (Violife)
  • A handful of shredded vegan cheddar (Violife)

Cajun Lime Mayo

  • ½ cup vegan mayo
  • Juice of ½ lime
  • 1 tsp onion powder
  • 1 tsp Cajun seasoning
  • ½ tsp paprika
  • ½ tsp garlic powder
  • ¼ tsp cumin
  • 3 tbsp soy milk (to thin)

To Wrap

  • Large burrito wraps

Instructions

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F.
  2. Add the olive oil, diced tofu, bell peppers, red onion, and jalapeños to a baking dish. Squeeze the juice of ½ lime over top, then sprinkle with the Cajun seasoning, onion powder, and salt. Toss everything together until well coated.
  3. Cover the dish tightly and bake for 20 minutes. Keeping it covered allows the tofu and veggies to steam and stay juicy while soaking up all the flavour.
  4. Remove from the oven and stir in the vegan mozzarella and cheddar.
  5. Cover again and bake for another 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and gooey.
  6. Mix all the Cajun lime mayo ingredients together until smooth (inferred - the caption only lists the mayo ingredients).
  7. Spoon some of the Cajun mayo into the burrito wrap and then the cheesy Cajun tofu mixture into burrito and wrap and then fry in a pan with a pinch of oil!

Note

From the caption of @plantbasedmace_'s reel, transcribed verbatim; vegan as written. The caption's ingredient list doesn't include the burrito wraps - added here so grocery lists catch them. The caption also lists the mayo ingredients without a mixing step (inferred above). Makes about 4 burritos.

Mayak Eggs (Korean Marinated Eggs)

15 min · serves 2
koreansideslunchhigh proteinspicy

Source: https://www.cookerru.com/mayak-eggs/

Ingredients

Eggs

  • 6 large eggs, at room temperature
  • 1 tbsp salt, for boiling
  • 1 tbsp white vinegar, for boiling

Marinade

  • 1/2 cup soy sauce
  • 1/2 cup water
  • 1/4 cup maple syrup or agave, regular honey works if you can't find it
  • 1/4 medium onion, diced
  • 1 green onion, diced
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 chili peppers, diced
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

To Serve

  • Green onions, chopped
  • Dried seaweed flakes
  • Sesame oil
  • Cooked rice or noodles

Instructions

  1. Add all the marinade ingredients to a bowl or container and mix well, scraping any sweetener off the bottom so it blends in.
  2. Bring a pot of water to a boil, then add the salt and vinegar. Lower the heat to a gentle simmer and lower in each egg one at a time. Simmer for 6 minutes for jammy soft boiled eggs, or 10 minutes for hard boiled. Cold eggs from the fridge need about a minute longer, though the temperature swing can crack the shells.
  3. Once the eggs are in, stir them gently in one direction for about 30 seconds to center the yolks. Meanwhile, prepare a large bowl of ice water.
  4. When the timer goes off, move the eggs straight into the ice bath and let them cool completely, at least 5 to 10 minutes.
  5. Gently peel the eggs and add them to the marinade. Cover tightly and refrigerate overnight, or at least 6 hours.
  6. To serve, place an egg over a bed of rice and top with green onion, seaweed flakes, and a drizzle of sesame oil. They are also great over a bowl of noodles.

Note

These keep about 3 to 4 days in the fridge and taste even better the next day as they soak up more flavor. Any leftover marinade is great for stir-frying vegetables, meat, or noodles.

Shopping list
produceonion, green onion, garlic, chili peppers
pantrysoy sauce, maple syrup (or agave), toasted sesame seeds, white vinegar, salt, sesame oil, dried seaweed flakes
proteineggs

From Cookerru (cookerru.com), recipe by Elle. The original uses honey; maple syrup or agave keeps it plant-based.

Chinese Braised Tofu with Green Onion (Scallion Tofu)

20 min · serves 2
tofuchinesebraiseddinnervegan

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/DYSVrq8xGfK/

Ingredients

Main

  • 4-5 green onions (about 50g), diagonally cut, white and green parts separated
  • 1 block firm tofu (about 400g)
  • 2 tbsp neutral oil
  • Red chilies (optional, for garnish and heat)

Sauce

  • 1.5 tbsp soy sauce
  • 0.5 tbsp dark soy sauce
  • 2 tsp vegan oyster sauce (mushroom-based; regular oyster sauce works if you can't find the vegan one)
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • ½ tbsp cornstarch
  • 2/3 cup water

Instructions

  1. Prepare the green onions by cutting them diagonally. Separate the white parts from the green parts. Use a spoon to cut the firm tofu into bite-sized pieces - the rough surface helps the tofu absorb more flavour.
  2. In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vegan oyster sauce, sugar, cornstarch, and water. Set aside.
  3. Heat a nonstick pan over medium heat. Add the neutral oil, then add the tofu. Pan-fry until both sides are golden, about 3-4 minutes per side.
  4. Make space in the pan and add the white parts of the green onion. Stir-fry for about 1 minute until fragrant.
  5. Stir the sauce again before adding it (the cornstarch may settle at the bottom), pour it in, cover, and simmer for 2-3 minutes until thick and glossy.
  6. Add the green parts of the green onion and gently toss everything together. Optional to add red chilies. Serve hot with steamed rice.

Tip

Using a spoon instead of a knife to cut the tofu creates rough edges that soak up more of the savoury brown sauce. Vegan note: the creator makes this vegan by swapping the oyster sauce for vegetarian (mushroom-based) oyster sauce, or using extra soy sauce with a little sugar.

Shopping list
producegreen onions/scallions, red chilies (optional)
pantryfirm tofu, neutral oil, soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vegan oyster sauce, sugar, cornstarch

From @thecrystalcookbook (Crystal Liang). Bang Bang Tofu

tofu
tofubang bangspicydinnervegan

Source: https://www.instagram.com/reel/Da2--KHvK2_/

Ingredients

Tofu

  • 1 block extra firm high-protein tofu
  • 1 tbsp nutritional yeast
  • ½ tbsp mushroom seasoning (optional - creator uses Trader Joe's)
  • 1 tsp white pepper
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 2 tbsp cornstarch
  • 1 tbsp oil
  • 1 tbsp soy sauce

Bang Bang Sauce

  • 2 tbsp vegan mayonnaise (regular works if you can't find the vegan one)
  • 3 tbsp sweet chili sauce
  • 2 tbsp sambal oelek chili garlic sauce
  • 1 tbsp sriracha
  • ½ tbsp rice vinegar
  • Chopped cilantro
  • Juice of ½ lemon
  • 1 tsp salt

To Serve

  • Jasmine rice
  • Sesame seeds
  • Extra cilantro
  • Fresh lemon

Instructions

  1. Tear the tofu into bite-sized pieces instead of cutting it into cubes. Those rough edges get extra crispy in the air fryer and hold onto more sauce.
  2. Add the nutritional yeast, mushroom seasoning (if using), white pepper, salt, cornstarch, oil, and soy sauce. Toss until every piece is evenly coated.
  3. Air fry at 400°F for 15-20 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through, until the tofu is golden brown and crispy.
  4. While the tofu cooks, whisk together the vegan mayo, sweet chili sauce, sambal oelek, sriracha, rice vinegar, cilantro, lemon juice, and salt until smooth.
  5. Toss the crispy tofu in the bang bang sauce until fully coated.
  6. Serve over a bed of jasmine rice and garnish with sesame seeds, extra cilantro, and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

Tip

Don't skip tearing the tofu - those craggy edges are the secret to getting the crispiest texture and soaking up every bit of that bang bang sauce.

Crispy Tofu Caesar Wrap

tofu
tofuwrapcaesarlunchvegan

Ingredients

Crispy Tofu Sticks

  • 1 block extra firm tofu
  • Flour, for dredging
  • Soy milk, for dredging
  • Breadcrumbs
  • Garlic powder
  • Onion powder
  • Paprika
  • Dill
  • Salt
  • Neutral oil (vegetable or canola), for frying

Vegan Caesar Dressing

  • 1/2 cup vegan mayo
  • 1.5 tsp lemon juice
  • 1 tsp Dijon
  • 1/2 tsp agave
  • 1/4 tsp vegan fish sauce (optional)
  • 1/2 tsp vegan Worcestershire (regular works if you can't find vegan)
  • 1/4 tsp Tabasco
  • 1 tsp chopped capers
  • 2 small cloves garlic, finely grated
  • 1/4 tsp black pepper
  • 1 tbsp soy milk (more if needed)
  • Optional splash of red wine vinegar

To Assemble

  • 1 large tortilla
  • Garlic vegan mayo (vegan garlic aioli)
  • Vegan mozzarella
  • Caesar salad (premixed)
  • Vegan bacon
  • Vegan parm

Instructions

Crispy Tofu Sticks

  1. Cut a block of extra firm tofu in half vertically, then slice into tofu sticks.
  2. Season breadcrumbs with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, dill, and salt.
  3. Set up 3 bowls: flour, soy milk, seasoned breadcrumbs.
  4. Coat each tofu stick: flour, soy milk, breadcrumbs, soy milk, breadcrumbs.
  5. Fry in neutral oil (vegetable or canola) until golden and crispy.

Vegan Caesar Dressing

  1. Mix all dressing ingredients together, adding more soy milk if needed. (Method inferred - the creator listed the dressing as ingredients only.)

Assemble the Wrap

  1. Spread garlic vegan mayo (creator used Hellmann's vegan garlic aioli) on a large tortilla.
  2. Add vegan mozzarella.
  3. Add Caesar salad (premix it all together!).
  4. Add extra vegan bacon.
  5. Add 3 crispy tofu sticks.
  6. Drizzle with extra Caesar dressing.
  7. Top with extra vegan parm.
  8. Roll tightly and cook in a frying pan for about 30 seconds per side, until lightly crisped.

Za'atar Green Olive Grilled Cheese

15 min · serves 1
vegetarianlunchcomfort foodquick

Ingredients

  • Italian bread, sliced
  • Softened butter
  • Castelvetrano green olives, pitted and roughly chopped
  • Fresh mozzarella, sliced
  • Za'atar seasoning

Instructions

  1. Butter both sides of each slice of bread, then generously sprinkle the buttered sides with za'atar.
  2. Heat a skillet over medium heat. Place the slices in the pan with one buttered side down and toast for 3–4 minutes, until golden and crisp. These toasted sides will become the inside of the sandwich.
  3. Flip the bread. Layer one slice with fresh mozzarella, chopped olives, and an extra sprinkle of za'atar. Top with the second slice of bread.
  4. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 3–4 minutes, until the cheese begins to melt. Flip carefully, cover again, and cook another 3–4 minutes until the bread is deeply golden and the cheese is completely melted.
  5. Slice and serve warm.
Shopping list

Crispy Miso Smashed Potato Salad

45 min · serves 4
saladspicymeal prep

Potatoes

  • 10-12 baby potatoes
  • salt (for the boiling water)
  • olive oil, for drizzling
  • salt, black pepper, paprika

Salad

  • 1/2 cucumber, thinly sliced
  • 2-3 tbsp fresh coriander (cilantro), chopped
  • spring onion, sliced
  • 1 tbsp white sesame seeds
  • 1 tbsp black sesame seeds

Miso Sauce

  • 3 tbsp of mayo
  • 3 tbsp of yoghurt
  • 1-2 tbsp chilli crisp
  • 1 tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 1/2 tbsp miso paste
  • 1 tbsp rice wine vinegar
  • 1/2 tbsp garlic powder

Instructions

  1. Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft and cooked through.

  3. Preheat the oven to 190C / 375F.
  4. Lay the potatoes on a parchment-lined baking sheet and smash each one down flat.
  5. Season with salt, pepper and paprika, then drizzle olive oil over the top.
  6. Bake for 15 minutes, or until crispy - timing varies with potato size and oven.
  7. Mix all the sauce ingredients in a bowl. Add the chilli crisp a little at a time if you cannot take much heat.
  8. Add the cucumber, coriander, spring onion, sesame seeds and crispy smashed potatoes to the sauce and mix well.

Tofu Burrata Sandwich

35 min · serves 2
veganlunchhigh proteintofu

Tofu

  • 1/2 block tofu (fava bean tofu, soy-free)
  • 1 tbsp avocado oil
  • pinch salt
  • black pepper
  • garlic powder
  • smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp coconut aminos

Cashew Burrata

  • 1 cup raw cashews, soaked 25 min in hot water (drained & rinsed)
  • ~1/2 cup water (blend to burrata consistency)
  • squeeze of lemon juice
  • 1.5 tbsp nutritional yeast
  • pinch salt

Cilantro Chimichurri

  • big handful fresh parsley
  • 1/2 cup fresh cilantro
  • 1 garlic clove
  • lemon zest
  • 2 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 tbsp red wine vinegar
  • 1 tsp red pepper flakes
  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • salt & pepper to taste
  • 2/3 cup olive oil

Assembly

  • bread (not specified in original - add your choice)

Instructions

  1. Slice the tofu into cutlets. Heat the avocado oil in a pan over medium heat. Season the tofu with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and coconut aminos. Cook 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and lightly crispy.
  2. Cashew burrata: blend the soaked, drained cashews with the water, lemon juice, and nutritional yeast until smooth and creamy. Adjust the amount of water to get a burrata-like consistency.
  3. Cilantro chimichurri: combine the parsley, cilantro, garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, red pepper flakes, oregano, salt, pepper, and olive oil until smooth.
  4. Spread a generous layer of cashew burrata on the bread. Add the cooked tofu slices, a handful of arugula, and ~1/2 cup sun-dried or roasted cherry tomatoes, then drizzle with cilantro chimichurri and sprinkle on extra burrata if you like. Close the sandwich and serve immediately.

  • 3 green onions, greens and whites separated
  • 3 to 4 large shiitake mushrooms, sliced
  • 1/2 cup Korean squash or zucchini
  • 1 cup Yukon gold potatoes (or any potatoes)
  • 3 tbsp doenjang
  • 2 tbsp soup soy sauce
  • 2 to 3 cups vegetable stock
  • 2 2-inch squares dashima (dried kelp)
  • 16 oz tofu (soft, medium, firm, or extra firm), sliced
  • 1 green chili pepper or jalapeño, seeded and thinly sliced

To Serve

  • Steamed white rice

Instructions

  1. To a large ddukbaeggi (Korean clay pot) or medium Dutch oven over low heat, add sesame oil, olive oil, and gochugaru. Use chopsticks or a wooden spoon to stir the gochugaru in the oil so that it doesn't burn until it begins to foam (about 1 to 2 minutes). Then, add the garlic, onion, green onion (white parts only), mushrooms, zucchini, and potatoes. Sauté the vegetables in the chili-infused oil until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
  2. Add the doenjang and stir until the vegetables are evenly coated. Then, deglaze the pot with soy sauce. Again, stir the vegetables so they are evenly coated. Add vegetable stock and raise the heat to medium-high. Add your dashima and bring your soup to a boil before reducing your heat to medium. Allow your soup to cook for an additional 10 minutes, until your potatoes are fork tender.
  3. Add your tofu and green chili pepper and cook for an additional 5 minutes, giving your tofu some time to suck up all the flavors. Remove the dried kelp and garnish with green onion (green parts).

💡 Stir the gochugaru into the oil low and slow until it foams but doesn't burn - that toasted chili base is what gives the stew its deep flavor.

Sautéed Lentil Bowl

35 min · serves 2
veganlunchdinnerbowlhigh proteinmeal prep

Ingredients

  • 1 cup dry green lentils, rinsed well
  • 3 cups water
  • 1 vegetable bouillon cube
  • 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, divided
  • 1 tsp cumin seeds
  • 1 tsp red pepper flakes (optional)
  • ½ medium red onion, thinly sliced
  • 3 cloves garlic, sliced or crushed
  • ½ tsp coriander
  • 1 small zucchini, thinly sliced (or bell pepper)
  • 5 sprigs fresh thyme, de-stemmed
  • Chili oil, for serving
  • Salt and pepper to taste

To Serve

  • Hummus
  • Rice
  • Chili oil drizzle

Instructions

  1. Add lentils, water, and bouillon cube to a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until tender, 15–17 minutes. Drain any remaining liquid and set aside.
  2. While the lentils finish up, warm a large skillet over medium heat. Add ½ tbsp of the olive oil, then the cumin seeds and red pepper flakes. Sauté about 1 minute to toast the cumin.
  3. Add the onion with a pinch of salt and sauté until softened. Splash in a little water or broth to deglaze if needed.
  4. Add the garlic and coriander, stirring frequently for about 1 minute until fragrant.
  5. Add the zucchini and sauté until the slices start to brown and soften.
  6. Add the remaining ½ tbsp oil, the cooked lentils, and thyme. Sauté everything together for 3–4 minutes to coat the lentils. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  7. To serve, smear a generous layer of hummus on your plate, top with the lentils, and finish with a drizzle of chili oil. Serve with rice on the side.
💡
The hummus base is the move here — don't skip it. It makes the whole bowl feel way more complete.

Jalapeño Tofu Breakfast Tacos

35 min · serves 4
veganbreakfasttacosspicy
📢
Remind anyone who slept in that you cooked breakfast SO THE DISHES ARE ALL THEM.

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp grapeseed or olive oil
  • 2 red potatoes, sliced into ⅛-inch rounds
  • ½ tsp salt
  • 2 tsp smoked paprika, divided
  • 2 tsp cumin, divided
  • ⅓ cup veggie broth or water
  • 1–2 jalapeños, sliced (to taste)
  • 1 red onion, sliced
  • 12 oz firm silken tofu
  • ¼ cup nooch* (nutritional yeast)
  • 1 tsp chili powder
  • 2 garlic cloves, thinly sliced
  • 1 cup cherry tomatoes, sliced
  • 1 tbsp Braggs Aminos or soy sauce
  • Juice of 1 lime
  • ¼ cup fresh cilantro, chopped

To Serve

  • Tortillas (warmed)
  • Salsa, hot sauce, guacamole, sliced jalapeños, cilantro

Instructions

💛
*Nooch = nutritional yeast, if you're not cool like that.
  1. Heat the oil in a large lidded pan over medium heat. Add the potatoes and salt, tossing to coat. Stir for about 3 minutes to warm through.
  2. Sprinkle over 1 tsp each of smoked paprika and cumin. Mix to coat, pour in the broth, stir, and put the lid on. Cook 5–7 minutes until potatoes have softened and the broth is mostly absorbed.
  3. Add the onion and jalapeño straight into the pan with the potatoes. Sauté everything together until the onion is translucent and the jalapeño has softened, about 5 minutes.
  4. Crumble in the tofu and sprinkle over the nooch, remaining smoked paprika, cumin, and chili powder. Toss to coat everything in the spices.
  5. Add the garlic, cherry tomatoes, and Braggs. Cook another 4 minutes until the tomatoes soften and everything is nicely combined.
  6. Finish with lime juice and cilantro, taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately with warmed tortillas and all the fixins.

Dressing

20 Min Thai Basil Tofu

20 min · serves 2
vegandinnerquickspicyhigh protein

Tofu

  • 1 block medium firm tofu
  • 1 tbsp light soy sauce
  • Cornstarch / cornflour — enough to coat
♨️
Air fry at 400°F for ~5 minutes until crispy.

Sauce

  • 1 tbsp ginger paste
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 2 tbsp light soy sauce
  • ½ tbsp dark soy sauce
  • 1 tbsp vegetarian oyster sauce
  • 1 tbsp sugar (or sweetener of choice)
  • 1 tbsp chili crisp
  • ⅓ cup water
  • 1 birds eye red chilli — adjust to your spice tolerance
  • 8–10 fresh Thai basil leaves

Serve With

  • Steamed white or brown rice
  • Noodles of your choice

Instructions

  1. Cube the tofu, toss with soy sauce, and coat lightly in cornstarch.
  2. Air fry at 400°F for 5 minutes until golden and slightly crispy. Set aside.
  3. Combine all sauce ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir and let it reduce for a couple of minutes.
  4. Add the air-fried tofu into the sauce. Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and coats the tofu.
  5. Turn off the heat and stir in the Thai basil leaves — the residual heat wilts them perfectly without killing the fragrance.
  6. Serve immediately over rice or noodles.

Potato & Chickpea Curry

75 min · serves 4
vegandinnercurrycomfort foodspicy
⚠️
Make the Cashew Cream, Cilantro Sauce, and Spice Blend BEFORE you start anything else. Don't be a hero.

Cashew Cream

💅
Optional, kind of. If you want real thick, creamy goodness make it from scratch. If you are a ratchet bitch without a taste for the finer things in life, you can get it canned or whatever.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup raw cashews
  • About ½ cup water

Instructions

  1. Boil some water.
  2. Put your cashews in a heat-safe container (Pyrex measuring glass works great).
  3. Pour boiling water over the cashews until fully covered. Let sit 15 minutes, then drain.
  4. Once cooled, blend with about ½ cup fresh water. Should be thick enough to stick to the back of a spoon. Add a touch more water if it won't blend, but keep it thiqqq.
  5. Scrape into a container or mason jar and set aside.

Spicy Cilantro Sauce

🌿
Again optional, but soooo good. Don't be a bitch — just make it. Make extra and jar it up. Goes well with a lot of stuff, keeps up to 1 week in the fridge.

Ingredients

  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • ¼ tsp ground coriander
  • ¾ tsp coarse sea salt, plus more to taste
  • 1 cup tightly packed fresh cilantro (chopped a little before blending)
  • 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice
  • ½ jalapeño (or a whole one if you aren't a bitch)

Instructions

  1. Combine garlic, olive oil, coriander, and salt in a small skillet.
  2. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook until garlic is fragrant, about 1½ minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.
  3. Transfer oil mixture to a blender. Add cilantro, lemon juice, jalapeño, and ¼ cup water. Blend until smooth.
  4. Season with salt as needed. Use immediately or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 1 week.

Spice Blend

🌶️
Non-negotiable. The whole dish is centered around this. Don't fuck it up.

Ingredients (makes ~5 tsp)

  • ¾ tsp salt
  • 1 tsp ground turmeric
  • 1 tsp coriander (seeds or ground)
  • ¾ tsp cumin
  • ¾ tsp fenugreek seeds
  • ¼ tsp brown mustard (seeds or ground) — DRY. Do NOT use the condiment.
  • ¼ tsp ground cinnamon
  • 1 whole clove

Instructions

  1. Get a small pan going on extra low heat.
  2. Add all spices and toast until fragrant, about 1 minute.
  3. Scrape into a spice grinder and grind down. Set aside.

The Curry

Ingredients

  • 1 can chickpeas (garbanzo beans for the uninitiated)
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 1 lb Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and cut into ½-inch cubes
  • 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
  • Freshly ground white pepper (rainbow or black if you're uncultured)
  • 1 fennel bulb (8–10 oz), trimmed (fronds reserved), quartered, cored, finely chopped — USE THE ACTUAL VEGETABLE, NOT JUST THE SEEDS
  • ¾ tsp to 1 tbsp seeded minced habanero chile (your call)
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 3 cups vegetable stock
  • 1 cup cashew cream (you made it, right?)
  • Fresh cilantro, for topping
  • Fresh lime juice, for finishing

Instructions

  1. Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. Toss potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp salt, and white pepper. Spread on baking sheet in a single layer.
  3. Roast until tender and golden on the edges, 25–30 minutes. Set aside.
  4. In a large pot with a lid, warm remaining 2 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat. Add fennel and sauté until softened, 4–5 minutes.
  5. Add garlic and habanero. Sauté until garlic is fragrant, 3–4 minutes.
  6. Stir in the spice blend and cook, stirring, for about 2 minutes.
  7. Stir in tomato paste until well combined.
  8. Pour in stock and cashew cream. Add the potatoes and chickpeas. Stir well.
  9. Reduce heat to medium-low, partially cover, and simmer about 20 minutes — stirring occasionally and scraping the bottom — until thickened and flavors have melded. Season with salt.
  10. Serve over rice. Top with cilantro sauce, fresh cilantro, fennel fronds, and a big squeeze of lime juice.
🏆
You did it. Now eat.

Quinoa

  • [ ] 1 cup quinoa, washed thoroughly
  • [ ] 1¾ cup water
  • [ ] 1 tsp salt

Tofu Feta

  • [ ] 1 block firm or extra firm tofu
  • [ ] Juice from 1 lemon
  • [ ] ¼ cup olive oil
  • [ ] 1–2 tsp salt
  • [ ] 1 tsp chili flakes
  • [ ] 1 tsp dried oregano
  • [ ] 1 tbsp nutritional yeast (optional)

Salad

  • [ ] 3 Persian cucumbers
  • [ ] 15 cherry tomatoes
  • [ ] 1 red onion
  • [ ] ¼ bunch cilantro
  • [ ] 2 tbsp olive oil
  • [ ] Salt and pepper to taste

  • [ ] 1 batch homemade hummus
  • [ ] Kalamata olives
  • [ ] Freshly ground black pepper
  • [ ] Sumac

👩‍🍳 Directions

Quinoa

  1. Rinse the quinoa under running water.

  4. Remove from heat and let sit covered for 10 more minutes. Fluff with a fork.

  1. Cut tofu into small cubes and place in a jar or container.
  2. Add lemon juice, olive oil, salt, chili flakes, oregano, and nutritional yeast.
  3. Stir or shake to coat evenly.
  4. Marinate at least 15 minutes, or refrigerate ahead for extra flavour.

  1. Dice cucumbers, quarter tomatoes, thinly slice onion, chop cilantro.

  2. Top with salad, ½ cup hummus, tofu feta, and kalamata olives.
  3. Drizzle with olive oil and finish with black pepper and sumac.
  4. Serve and enjoy!
